changed.title: Disjoint blocks of cyclic SAT table rows can each query any entry of one encoded matrix
changed.statement:
∀ d b p q : ℕ,
  let w := d + 1
  let D := Fin d → Bool
  let B := b + 1
  let L := 3 * w * 2 ^ d
  let n := L + B * w + p * w + q * (w + 1)
  let hn : 0 < n := by dsimp [n, L, B, w]; positivity
  let Pattern := Fin (w + 1) → Bool
  ∃ (ctx : (D → D → Bool) → Fin n → Pattern → Bool)
    (probe : D → D → Fin w → Pattern → Bool),
    (∀ M N i, L ≤ i.val → ctx M i = ctx N i) ∧
    ∀ (A : D → D → Bool) (u v : D) (h : Fin B),
      let start := L + h.val * w
      let row := fun (i : Fin n) (pat : Pattern) =>
        if start ≤ i.val ∧ i.val < start + w then
          probe u v (Fin.ofNat (d + 1) (i.val - start)) pat
        else ctx A i pat
      let ok := fun (word : Fin n → Bool) => ∀ s : Fin n,
        row s (fun k => word ⟨(s.val + k.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true
      (Finset.univ.filter ok).card = (A u v).toNat
changed.unlocks: lets each disjoint block distinguish every pair of matrix contents for the formula leaf count
changed.context: Use L-lib-383 for the matrix prefix. Each resting block copies the dropped bit w times, inducing identity. In the selected block require the initial window to be (1,v) and append (0,u) over w steps. This is a unique path between those endpoints. Closing the cycle therefore requires a path in the matrix prefix from (0,u) to (1,v), whose count is A(u,v). Each padding block is a unique identity, by w copies or w+1 steps appending the window parity. Paths returning to their start spell indexed words.

changed.title: It is false that: Table 1a, 5 by 5, mask 16124928: represented by an AND/OR circuit of fan-in two with at most 6 gates
changed.statement: ¬ (PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v : Fin 5 => (16124928 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 6)
changed.unlocks: Proving it shows that a listed statement is false.
changed.context: Every singleton rejects by monotonicity and an opposite zero. Each of the 7 vertices of positive degree must therefore be read. Normalize the live cone, folding constants and missing or forward operands. With at most 6 gates there are at most 12 operand slots, exactly 7 forced raw reads and at least one use for each nonoutput gate. Equality forces two operands per gate, one use per leaf and one per nonoutput gate. Apply the read-once three-corner theorem. Rows 4 and 2, columns 0 and 2 have three positive corners and a negative fourth.

changed.title: It is false that: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 816112 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 10 gates
changed.unlocks: Proving it shows that a listed statement is false.
changed.context: Columns zero and one are twins, as are four and five. Delete columns one and five successively. Each deleted column has a positive partner and a zero, so its input wire must occur by monotonicity and the zero singleton at its positive partner. Each deletion saves at least one gate by transposed vertex restriction. In the remaining matrix take rows 1,2,0,3 and columns 0,4,2,3. Their row masks are 13,5,2,1. The resulting 4 by 4 mask is 4701 and its lower bound excludes eight gates.

changed.title: It is false that: Some AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 5 gates represents one of two named 5 by 5 graphs (masks 16235582, 16236078) on the one-a-side promise
changed.statement:
¬ (∃ M ∈ ([16235582, 16236078] : List ℕ), ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 5 ∧
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => M.testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C)
